sections.title: R9 — публичный PHP API пакета: snapshot vs Eloquent, BC, миграции, конфиг, ошибки, события
sections.text:
Запрос:
Best practices for the PUBLIC PHP API of a Laravel package (SemVer, 1.0 freeze), drawing on official docs and well-known packages (Laravel Cashier, Laravel Horizon/Pulse, Spatie laravel-medialibrary, laravel-permission, laravel-activitylog, Filament plugins, Symfony BC promise, PHP-FIG, Stripe PHP SDK, AWS SDK for PHP). Cite sources; separate documented facts from recommendations.

1. Returning Eloquent models from the public API vs immutable read DTOs/value objects. Risks: hosts calling ->save()/->update()/->delete() bypassing domain invariants and authorization, every column becoming a BC promise, serialization leaks (toArray/JSON). Mitigations used in practice: model-level guards (preventing writes outside a unit of work), @internal attributes, read-only models, DTO mapping cost. Recommendation for a drive package whose models are Node/File/FileRevision/Document/Drive and whose writes must go through authorized operations.
2. Symfony-style BC promise: what is covered (classes, interfaces, method signatures, constructor params, enums cases, exception classes/codes, events, config keys, database schema, migrations) and how to mark internal (@internal, final, namespaces). How to evolve enums (adding cases breaks exhaustive match), DTOs (named args, adding optional params), interfaces meant for implementation by users vs for calling.
3. Package-shipped migrations: loadMigrationsFrom vs publishable migrations; upgrade migrations across major versions; idempotent/guarded migrations; how Cashier/Horizon/Telescope/medialibrary handle schema evolution; recommending "expand-migrate-contract".
4. Configuration stability: typed config objects, validation at boot, deprecations with normalizers, env names.
5. Extension points: registries with freeze-after-boot, tagged services, contract test kits for implementers.
6. Errors: exception hierarchy + stable machine codes + RFC 9457 mapping; retryability flags.
7. Events: Laravel events as public API (payload classes immutable, after-commit dispatch), naming.
Give a checklist for "1.0 freeze readiness".


Ответ:
For your drive package, freeze a narrow contract: authorized operations accept explicit actor/context and IDs or command DTOs; reads return immutable, deliberately shaped snapshots; Eloquent models remain internal persistence objects. Adopt Symfony-style PHP compatibility rules, but explicitly extend your promise to error codes, event payloads, configuration, and supported database-upgrade paths—Symfony’s PHP rules do not automatically define those obligations.
Below, “Documented” identifies behavior supported by official documentation or first-party repositories. “Recommendation” describes the policy I would choose for your package; it is not a claim that the cited packages implement it.

## 1. Models versus read DTOs


## Documented practice

Returning mutable models is an established Laravel-package pattern, not inherently a design mistake:
These examples establish that model-centric APIs can be successful. They do not establish that such APIs preserve your stronger requirement: every drive write must pass an authorized domain operation.

## Actual risks

- Direct persistence bypasses the intended command boundary. A caller can mutate attributes and call save(), or use query-level updates/deletes. Laravel documents that mass updates/deletes bypass the corresponding per-model events. Consequently, an observer is not a comprehensive enforcement boundary.
- Serialization exposes more than a deliberate read contract. Eloquent recursively serializes attributes and loaded relationships; changing what is loaded can change the output. $hidden and $visible control serialization, but callers can change those settings on an instance.
- Persistence structure becomes observable. Returning a model exposes attribute names, casts, relationships, query builders, connection behavior, and inherited Eloquent methods. “Every column becomes a BC promise” is not literally automatic: your policy can exclude undocumented attributes. Nevertheless, exposing them makes accidental dependencies likely and compatibility disputes harder to resolve.
- Read access and write authorization become confused. A model retrieved through an authorized read is not evidence that a later mutation is authorized. Permissions, tenant membership, parent location, and revision head may have changed.
- Database identity and domain identity become coupled. Hosts may start depending on your primary-key representation, relationship layout, or storage-specific fields.
The last three points are architectural analysis, not claims that all the example packages suffer those failures.

## Mitigation comparison

The final three rows are proposed design techniques. The cited package documentation does not establish a common Laravel-package standard for comprehensive read-only models or unit-of-work write guards.

## Recommendation for your entities

Keep Node, File, FileRevision, Document, and Drive Eloquent classes under something like:
```
Vendor\Drive\Internal\Persistence\Eloquent
```
Mark them @internal, exclude them explicitly in the BC policy, and do not return them from public operations.
Expose public read types such as:
```
NodeSnapshot FileSnapshot FileRevisionSnapshot DocumentSnapshot DriveSnapshot
```
Recommended rules:
- Use final DTOs with readonly properties where your PHP baseline permits.
- Use immutable nested values, including DateTimeImmutable; readonly properties alone do not guarantee a deeply immutable object graph.
- Return explicit fields, not attributesToArray() copied wholesale.
- Do not embed Eloquent models, lazy relations, query builders, storage credentials, or internal blob paths.
- Separate document summaries from large content/revision payloads.
- Return a package-defined page/result type rather than leaking an Eloquent collection or builder.
- Treat snapshots as point-in-time observations, not authorization capabilities.
- Accept IDs and expected versions in writes; reauthorize and recheck invariants inside the operation.
Illustrative API, not an existing package API:
```
$node = $drive->nodes()->get( actor: $actor, nodeId: $nodeId, ); $renamed = $drive->nodes()->rename( actor: $actor, nodeId: $node->id, name: 'Report.pdf', expectedVersion: $node->version, );
```
DTO mapping has an allocation and transformation cost, but do not assume it dominates. Benchmark representative listings and document reads; avoid hydrating full models or relations merely to produce a small projection.
As defense in depth, a unit-of-work guard may reject instance writes outside authorized operations. Make its context scoped and cleared with finally; do not use a process-global “writes enabled” flag in long-lived workers. Database constraints remain necessary for structural invariants.
Crucially, this is an API boundary, not a security sandbox against the host application. A host with your database credentials can issue SQL directly.

## 2. Define the BC promise


## What Symfony actually promises

Symfony covers supported use of public classes, interfaces, methods, properties, constructors, and—in classes intended for extension—protected members. Internal and experimental code are excluded; security fixes can justify compatibility breaks. Symfony also distinguishes changes safe for final classes from changes that break subclasses or interface implementations.
A particularly important exception: Symfony generally does not cover parameter names for named arguments, except constructor parameters of Attribute classes. Do not describe “Symfony-style BC” as automatically guaranteeing named arguments.
Stripe provides a complementary precedent: its SDK versioning documentation identifies required-parameter changes, type/property/method changes, and renamed exception classes as major-version changes. It also documents SDK/API-version coupling; package versioning and remote protocol versioning are separate concerns.

## Recommended coverage matrix

Publish this before 1.0:
These are your proposed obligations, not a verbatim Symfony policy. Database schema, Laravel configuration, and application-event semantics need their own written rules.

## Internal marking

Use three complementary signals:
```
namespace Vendor\Drive\Internal\Persistence; /** @internal */ final class NodeRepository { }
```
- Internal\… communicates architectural intent.
- @internal supports documentation/static-analysis conventions.
- final prevents inheritance where that is not supported.
A PHP attribute can supplement your tooling, but do not assume a universal native #[Internal] access-control mechanism. Nor does placing a class in an internal namespace alone create a compatibility policy.
Do not add final or retroactively label an already-supported extension point internal in a minor release to escape existing promises. Symfony expressly treats making an extensible class final as a BC issue.

## Enums

PHP requires match to handle the supplied value; an unhandled value raises UnhandledMatchError. Adding an enum case can therefore break callers whose matches were exhaustive over the previous cases.
Recommendation:
- For a closed NodeKind enum, treat new reachable cases as major changes.
- For extensible document/provider types, prefer a validated string-backed value object or registry key.
- If you permit minor-release enum additions, say so before 1.0 and require fallback handling.
- Do not assume an Unknown case automatically solves exhaustive matching: callers still need a policy for future cases.
- Freeze backed values independently from display labels.

## DTO evolution and named arguments

Symfony allows trailing optional constructor arguments, but its named-argument exception remains important.
For your API, I recommend a stronger, simpler promise: public parameter names are stable.
Safe-looking additions still need scrutiny:
- A trailing optional DTO constructor parameter can preserve existing construction.
- A new serialized field changes the output shape; callers must be told whether output is extensible.
- Making a field nullable or changing its default changes semantics.
- Adding optional parameters to a user-implemented interface can still break implementations.
- Queued or persisted serialized DTOs require compatibility beyond source-level constructor checks.
If callers should only receive a DTO, you may exclude construction from the public promise—but enforce/document that distinction clearly. PHPUnit offers a concrete precedent: its event value objects promise compatibility for public query methods, not their constructors.

## Extension interfaces

PHP-FIG’s accepted PSRs provide standardized interoperability interfaces; draft PSRs are explicitly subject to change. This supports using accepted contracts where they fit, not claiming PHP-FIG defines your whole package’s BC policy.
For user implementations, prefer small capability interfaces. Add a new optional interface rather than a required method:
```
BlobStore ConditionalWriteBlobStore MultipartUploadBlobStore
```
Avoid “future-proof” interfaces with large arrays and vague semantics: fewer methods do not help if their behavioral contract is unspecified.

## 3. Migrations and configuration


## Migration ownership in practice

Laravel’s package documentation provides publishable migrations through publishesMigrations(), including timestamp adjustment on publication. loadMigrationsFrom() instead registers a package migration path; loading migrations is not the same as executing migrations during boot.
The history matters:
Publication provides host control, but also produces independently owned copies. Updating Composer dependencies does not update an already-published migration/configuration file.

## Recommended migration policy

For an embeddable drive package, use publishable migrations as the default if hosts need connection, table-name, or identity customization. Offer package-loaded migrations only as an explicitly selected alternative; do not accidentally activate both.
Establish these rules:
- Never require hosts to edit an already-executed migration.
- Ship additive upgrade migrations and precise upgrade instructions.
- Test both fresh installation and upgrades from representative released schemas.
- Define which migration customizations are supported.
- Keep migration code independent of current mutable model behavior and renamed runtime services.
- Preserve migration identifiers sufficiently to prevent duplicate execution.
- Document database engines, locking implications, minimum schema state, and rollback limitations.
- Do not run DDL or backfills automatically during provider boot.
Idempotency needs precision. Laravel’s migration tracking is the primary “already applied” mechanism. Blanket hasTable()/hasColumn() guards can silently accept an incompatible schema.
Use guards only when multiple supported starting states are intentional. Validate the existing structure; fail visibly if it is wrong. Make data backfills independently resumable, with stable checkpoints and concurrency-safe writes.

## Expand-migrate-contract

- Expand: add new structures without removing old ones.
- Deploy compatible code: support the required overlap between old/new schema and application versions.
- Migrate: backfill in bounded, resumable batches; verify completeness.
- Switch: change authoritative reads/writes only after validation.
- Contract: remove obsolete structures after old workers and rollback windows are gone.
A major package release does not itself make destructive migrations safe. Queue workers, cached deployments, and incomplete backfills still need an operational transition.

## Configuration stability

Documented constraints:
- Laravel warns against closures in configuration because of config:cache.
- mergeConfigFrom() merges only the first array level, so nested defaults need special care.
- AWS SDK for PHP explicitly documents retry configuration precedence: client options, environment variables, then shared configuration. Its retry modes and limits have defined semantics.
- Keep the published Laravel configuration as cache-compatible arrays/scalars.
- Normalize it into an internal typed, immutable configuration object.
- Validate after host overrides are available and before the affected feature is used.
- Validate types, units, ranges, cross-field constraints, driver existence, and incompatible combinations.
- Do not require database/network availability just to build the configuration cache.
- Do not instantiate public command DTOs merely to represent infrastructure configuration.
For renamed keys, normalize old and new names to one canonical setting. Specify precedence and reject conflicting values where silent selection would be dangerous. Deprecate old names throughout the remaining major line, including environment aliases.
Treat changes to authorization defaults, retention, visibility, file limits, and retry behavior as semantic compatibility decisions—not merely configuration cleanup.

## 4. Extensions, errors, and events


## Extension points

Documented: Laravel supports tagged services and resolving groups through tagged()/giveTagged(). Filament panel plugins use explicit plugin objects and lifecycle integration, while standalone-plugin configuration belongs in the service provider.
- Register extension definitions during a documented registration phase.
- Freeze registries after all participating providers have completed registration/boot integration—not at an arbitrary point in your own provider’s boot().
- Reject late registrations with a clear error.
- Reject duplicate keys unless explicit replacement is supported.
- Define ordering, priority ties, and replacement rules.
- Keep registration separate from instantiation.
- Keep actor/tenant state out of process-wide registry definitions.
- Version/document tag names if third-party packages use them.
A freeze-after-boot registry is a proposed package discipline; it is not implied by Laravel tagging or Filament’s lifecycle.
Ship contract-test kits for user implementations. For example, a blob-store kit should test missing objects, conditional writes, streaming, cleanup, error translation, and idempotency. An actor adapter kit should test tenant isolation and fail-closed missing-actor behavior.
The behavioral specification is authoritative; passing a test kit is evidence, not a security certification.

## Exceptions and machine codes

Documented: Stripe treats exception-class renames as breaking SDK changes. AWS SDK for PHP exposes operation failures through exceptions and documents retry configuration separately.
Recommended hierarchy:
```
DriveException ├── ActorRequired ├── AccessDenied ├── ResourceNotFound ├── ValidationFailed ├── Conflict └── StorageFailure
```
Freeze catch categories and provide methods such as:
```
public function machineCode(): string; public function retryable(): bool; public function safeContext(): array;
```
Do not overload PHP’s integer Exception::getCode() with your string domain codes.
For example:
A retryability flag is advisory. A transient error does not establish that retrying a partially completed write is safe. Specify operation idempotency and outcome uncertainty separately; preserve underlying exceptions for diagnostics without leaking them through public serialization.
RFC 9457 defines application/problem+json, with type as the primary problem identifier. It supports extension members, requires clients to ignore unknown extensions, and warns against exposing internals through error details.
Map domain exceptions in an HTTP adapter, not in the domain core:
- Stable type URI.
- HTTP status appropriate to the transport’s authentication and disclosure policy.
- Human-readable title and detail.
- Stable extension code.
- Optional retryable, occurrence identifier, and safe validation details.
RFC 9457 does not standardize your code or retryable fields. Those are your extensions. Also, an “actor required” domain failure does not automatically imply every HTTP adapter should return 401: distinguish missing authentication from an integration failing to supply its actor.

## Events

Documented: Laravel’s ShouldDispatchAfterCommit delays dispatch until the active transaction commits and discards the event if that transaction fails. Laravel also warns that queued listeners can otherwise execute before transaction commit.
- Publish domain events, not raw Eloquent lifecycle events.
- Use immutable scalar/value-object payloads rather than mutable models.
- Name PHP events as completed facts: NodeRenamed, FileRevisionCreated, DocumentUpdated, DriveDeleted.
- Specify exactly when each fact occurs.
- Include stable entity/tenant IDs, event ID, actor identity, occurrence time, and relevant version.
- Include only minimal authorized data; avoid content, tokens, and storage secrets.
- Specify whether no-op operations emit events.
- Treat changing an event class/name or removing payload fields as breaking.
- Document whether adding fields and new event types is permitted in minor releases.
Laravel’s model serialization machinery is convenient, but a serialized/reloaded model is not the same thing as an immutable snapshot of event-time state.
After-commit dispatch solves rollback visibility; it does not establish durable delivery across a process crash. If durable external side effects are required, write an outbox record in the same transaction and publish asynchronously. Define duplicate handling and delivery guarantees separately from the PHP event API.
For persisted events, make payload-format compatibility an explicit promise. A new constructor default alone does not guarantee that old queued payloads deserialize correctly.

## 5. 1.0 freeze readiness

The following is a recommended release gate, not a checklist copied from any one package.

## Public surface

- A published BC policy enumerates supported classes, methods, DTOs, interfaces, errors, events, configuration, and upgrade paths.
- Internal namespaces and annotations are consistent; examples do not encourage internal APIs.
- Public classes are final unless inheritance is an intentional extension point.
- Named-argument support and constructor coverage are explicit.
- Enum domains are declared closed or extensible.
- Supported PHP/Laravel/database versions and dependency-drop policy are documented.

## Authorization and persistence

- No public result accidentally exposes writable Eloquent models or builders.
- Every write requires explicit actor/context, including jobs and CLI operations.
- Authorization is rechecked at execution time.
- Tenant isolation, optimistic concurrency, and structural invariants are tested.
- DTOs contain no mutable persistence objects or sensitive internal fields.
- Serialization uses explicit allowlists and has golden-contract tests.
- Model guards are described as defense in depth, not complete isolation.

## Installation and upgrades

- Migration ownership and publication/loading modes are unambiguous.
- Fresh installation and upgrades from released schema fixtures pass.
- Existing published configuration files receive correct defaults or actionable errors.
- Backfills are resumable and reject unsupported starting states.
- Destructive schema changes have an expand-migrate-contract plan.
- config:cache, long-lived workers, and supported deployment overlap are tested.
- Restore and rollback limitations are documented.

## Extension and behavior contracts

- User-implemented interfaces have a behavioral specification and test kit.
- Registry freeze timing, duplicate handling, replacement, and ordering are deterministic.
- Exception hierarchy, machine codes, and retry/idempotency semantics are documented.
- HTTP problem mappings do not leak internals.
- Event payloads, occurrence rules, after-commit behavior, and durability boundaries are documented.
- Old supported consumer fixtures still compile and pass behavior tests against the candidate release.
- Deprecations name the replacement and removal major; security exceptions to BC have a stated policy.
The decisive 1.0 test is not whether the database schema will never change. It is whether a host can use the documented API, implement the documented extensions, and upgrade through the documented procedure without depending on your persistence internals.

Sources:
1. [laravel](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/12.x/billing)
2. [spatie](https://spatie.be/docs/laravel-medialibrary/v11/basic-usage/retrieving-media)
3. [spatie](https://spatie.be/docs/laravel-permission/v8/upgrading)
4. [laravel](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/eloquent)
5. [laravel](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/12.x/eloquent-serialization)
6. [laravel](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/5.2/eloquent)
7. [symfony](https://symfony.com/doc/current/contributing/code/bc.html)
8. [php](https://www.php.net/manual/en/control-structures.match.php)
9. [phpunit](https://phpunit.de/backward-compatibility.html)
10. [laravel](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/11.x/upgrade)

sections.title: R10 — квоты (фрагмент таблицы)
sections.text:
Запрос:
For a multi-tenant Laravel drive package (soft trash with retention, quotas per drive, uploads via tus/S3 multipart, CAS blobs with ref-count GC, optional antivirus scanning with quarantine), compare official docs/specs: Google Drive (storage quota, trash 30 days, file size limits, abuse/virus download warnings), Box (upload sessions, preflight check, quarantine/malware deep scan "Box Shield", trash retention configurable), Dropbox (upload sessions, batch commit, content_hash), Microsoft Graph (createUploadSession, conflictBehavior fail/replace/rename, quota fields total/used/remaining/deleted/state normal/nearing/critical/exceeded), S3 (multipart limits, checksums, lifecycle abort incomplete multipart), tus protocol (creation, expiration, checksum, termination extensions). Cite docs.

1. Quota model: fields and states (Graph quota.state), what counts (trash, revisions, shared items), soft vs hard limits, per-tenant pooled quotas, recalculation/reconciliation jobs, and behaviour at limit (reject uploads but allow deletes/restores?).
2. Upload preflight (Box preflight, Graph conflictBehavior) and name-conflict policies on upload/copy/move/restore: fail|rename|replace and where "replace" creates a new revision; idempotency keys.
3. Malware handling: states (pending/clean/infected/failed/unscanned), what users see, owner/admin override download, rescans on signature updates, legacy content created before scanning existed.
4. Trash/retention configuration per tenant/container and admin "empty trash", hard-delete guarantees.
5. Limits configuration (max file size, max upload session lifetime, max parts, max children) and their error codes (413/507/409/429).
Give recommendations and a final table for a stable schema/config.


Ответ:
"Operation","Recommended behavior"
"New upload or copy","Reject if incremental charge cannot fit."
"Replace with a new revision","Reserve the full new revision size when old revisions remain chargeable."
"Soft delete","Allow; it does not free quota under the recommended accounting model."
"Hard purge","Allow unless retention/legal hold blocks it; release logical quota when references are durably removed."
"Restore trash","Allow when charge-neutral; still enforce ACL, conflict, and child-count rules."
"Restore under trash-excluded accounting","Reserve additional quota first; restoration can fail for insufficient space."
"Move within one quota account","Allow if charge-neutral."
"Move across drives","Atomically transfer charge and check destination sublimit; tenant-pool usage may remain unchanged."
"Download, cancel upload, rename","Do not block merely because storage quota is full."

sections.title: R10a — квоты и конфликты имён
sections.text:
Запрос:
Concise with official doc links (Microsoft Graph quota resource and conflictBehavior, Box preflight check and upload sessions, Google Drive storageQuota and keepRevisionForever, Dropbox WriteMode add/overwrite/update and autorename): (1) recommended quota fields/states for a drive package (total, used, deleted/trash, remaining, state normal|nearing|critical|exceeded), what is charged (all retained revisions? trash? logical bytes not dedup-discounted), soft vs hard limits, reconciliation job; (2) name-conflict policy for upload/copy/move/restore: fail | rename (suffix format "name (1).ext") | replace (= new revision of existing file, never delete+create), idempotency keys for uploads; which policy should be default for API vs UI.


Ответ:
Use a logical quota ledger and explicit conflict policies: API defaults to fail; ordinary UI uploads default to rename; replace must update the existing file’s content as a new revision, preserving its ID. Treat this as your package’s contract—not a universal provider contract: Microsoft Graph’s copy replace explicitly deletes the destination and its history.

## 1. Quota contract

Recommended fields, all byte counts stored as 64-bit integers:
For provider-backed storage, distinguish package counters from provider_used / provider_remaining: quotas may cover a user, organization, or multiple services rather than this drive alone. Graph documents unified storage for OneDrive Personal; Google’s storageQuota.usage covers all services and can reflect organizational pooled storage.

## States and enforcement

Recommended thresholds follow :
Graph defines exceeded strictly as usage exceeding capacity. Therefore, at exactly full, report critical but reject any positive-growth operation; do not use state alone for admission.
Recommended enforcement:
- Soft thresholds produce warnings; they do not reject writes.
- Hard admission checks atomically require used + reserved_bytes + positive_delta <= total.
- Unlimited quota returns normal; unknown/stale provider quota needs separate metadata, not a fabricated zero.
- Keep reads, purge, and non-growing metadata operations available when full.
- Keep per-file size, request-rate, and daily-upload limits separate from storage quota.
- Preflight is advisory; reserve capacity and recheck at commit. Box explicitly warns that a successful preflight does not guarantee a successful upload, and creating an upload session includes a preflight.

## 2. What gets charged

For your own managed storage, recommended policy:
- Charge the full logical size of every retained revision, including the head.
- Charge retained trash, including its revisions; moving to trash does not release quota.
- Release charges when purge/retention expiry makes content permanently unavailable.
- Do not discount compression, deduplication, or physical block sharing. Track physical storage separately.
- Do not count the same revision twice merely because it is both a head and retained forever.
These are package design choices, not claims that every provider accounts this way.
Example under your recommended policy: a 100 MB file replaced by a 120 MB revision consumes 220 MB while both revisions remain. Trashing it still consumes 220 MB; permanently purging both releases 220 MB.
Recommended reconciliation job: maintain a transactional revision-level ledger, then periodically rebuild totals from authoritative retained-revision metadata. Compare against incremental counters, repair drift with an audit record, expire abandoned reservations, and keep provider aggregates as a separately timestamped observation. Do not overwrite local counters using a stale provider snapshot—Box documents aggregate delays of up to 24 hours for larger changes, sometimes longer.

## 3. Name-conflict contract

Resolve conflicts within (drive_id, parent_id, normalized_name), using one documented Unicode/case-normalization rule and atomic uniqueness enforcement.

Sources:
1. [learn.microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/driveitem-copy?view=graph-rest-1.0)
2. [Microsoft Graph’s quota resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/quota?view=graph-rest-1.0)
3. [storageQuota](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/about)
4. [keepRevisionForever](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/files/update)
5. [box](https://support.box.com/hc/en-us/articles/360043695334-Storage-Usage-Or-File-Count-In-My-Account-Is-Incorrect)

sections.title: R10b — вредоносный контент (фрагмент)
sections.text:
Запрос:
Concise with official doc links (Google Drive virus scan warnings and abuse flags, Box Shield malware deep scan and download restrictions, Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Safe Attachments / SharePoint infected file blocking (DisallowInfectedFileDownload), Nextcloud antivirus app modes, ClamAV signature updates): recommended malware state model for a drive package (pending, clean, infected, error, not_scanned), what users and admins can do in each state (download override with audit), rescanning on signature updates and for legacy unscanned content, scan result provenance (engine, signature version, scanned_at), and behavior of preview/export/copy/share for non-clean content.


Ответ:
Use a five-state malware model on immutable file content, with fail-closed delivery by default and a separately authorized, audited raw-download override. Keep malware verdicts, scan freshness, and abuse/moderation flags separate; the rules below are package recommendations, not claims that every vendor implements them.

## Official vendor behavior

Sources:
1. [Security guidance](https://support.google.com/drive/answer/141702?hl=en-fj)
2. [Abuse review](https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2463328?hl=en)
3. [API files.get](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/files/get)
4. [Malicious Content Detection](https://support.box.com/hc/en-us/articles/46976541627411-Malicious-Content-Detection-Rule)

sections.title: Принятые решения и отклонённое
sections.text: Принято решениями D38–D50 (см. каждое). Отложено (T2, аддитивно после 1.0): таблица рендиций (миниатюры/превью — аддитивная таблица + источник рёбер CAS), blob_checksums для md5/crc32c, envelope-шифрование по tenant (blobs.encryption_key_id уже зарезервирован), legal hold/retention lock, передача владения, ручной порядок детей, closure-таблица и материализованные ACL (runtime-оценка остаётся канонической), last_viewed_at/recents. Отклонено: отдельный public_id (D38), трим имён, deny для конечных пользователей, глобальная дедупликация, «replace» как delete+create (replace = новая ревизия того же файла).
